drivingQuestion: When does one begin to request rain, and does the sixtieth day count as within or after the sixty days?
outcomeNote: Rav Pappa rules the sixtieth day counts as after sixty, like Rav

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל. תַּנְיָא, חֲנַנְיָה אוֹמֵר: וּבַגּוֹלָה, עַד שִׁשִּׁים בַּתְּקוּפָה. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כַּחֲנַנְיָה.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «Rabbi Elazar said: The halakha is in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabban Gamliel,» that one does not begin to request rain until the seventh of Marḥeshvan. It «is taught» in a baraita that «Ḥananya says: And in the Diaspora» one does not begin to request rain «until sixty» days «into the season,» i.e., sixty days after the autumnal equinox. «Rav Huna bar Ḥiyya said» that «Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with» the opinion of «Ḥananya.»

segments.he: אִינִי?! וְהָא בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מִשְּׁמוּאֵל: מֵאֵימַת מַדְכְּרִינַן ״וְתֵן טַל וּמָטָר״? אֲמַר לְהוּ: מִכִּי מְעַיְּילִי צִיבֵי לְבֵי טָבוּת רִישְׁבָּא! דִּילְמָא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי חַד שִׁיעוּרָא הוּא.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Is that so? But they raised a dilemma before Shmuel: From when does one mention: And give dew and rain? He said to them: From when they bring wood into the house of Tavut the bird hunter [rishba].» This is apparently a different date than that mentioned by Ḥananya. The Gemara suggests: «Perhaps this and that are one measure» of time, i.e., Shmuel merely provided a sign of sixty days after the autumnal equinox.

segments.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: יוֹם שִׁשִּׁים, כְּלִפְנֵי שִׁשִּׁים אוֹ כִּלְאַחַר שִׁשִּׁים? תָּא שְׁמַע, רַב אָמַר: יוֹם שִׁשִּׁים כִּלְאַחַר שִׁשִּׁים, וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: יוֹם שִׁשִּׁים כְּלִפְנֵי שִׁשִּׁים.
segments.en: «A dilemma was raised before» the Sages: Is the «sixtieth day» itself treated as part «of» the period «before» the «sixtieth» day «or» is it included «in» the period «after» the «sixtieth» day? The Gemara answers. «Come» and «hear» that there is a dispute in this regard. «Rav said:» The «sixtieth day» is part «of» the period «after» the «sixtieth» day, «and Shmuel said:» The «sixtieth day» is part «of» the period «before» the «sixtieth.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: וְסִימָנָךְ עִלָּאֵי בָּעוּ מַיָּא, תַּתָּאֵי לָא בָּעוּ מַיָּא. אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, הִלְכְתָא: יוֹם שִׁשִּׁים כִּלְאַחַר שִׁשִּׁים.
segments.en: «Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: And your mnemonic» to remember the divergent opinions is: «Those above require water; those below do not require water.» Since water flows downward, those who live in low places receive their water from above and are generally in less need of additional water. Accordingly, Shmuel, who lived in the lowlands of Babylonia, ruled that one begins to request for rain later, whereas Rav, who studied in Eretz Yisrael, which is higher in elevation and has a greater need for rain, stated an earlier date. «Rav Pappa said: The halakha is» that the «sixtieth day» is part «of» the period «after» the «sixtieth» day, as stated by «Rav,» and therefore one begins to mention the request for rain on the sixtieth day after the autumnal equinox.
